extracted.intended_audience: businesses and legal counsel preparing comments to the FTC on the proposed noncompete clause rule
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for stakeholders (particularly businesses) on preparing and submitting comments to the FTC's proposed Non-Compete Clause Rule, covering deadlines, required technical/formal information, recommended evidentiary support, and specific topics the FTC requests input on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Deadlines / Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment Period: January 8 – April 19, 2023 (original deadline mentioned: March 20, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments within the stated comment period; note that this was the only opportunity for businesses to provide input on the proposed rule. Timely filing is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Methods / Filing Channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical Mail: Federal Trade Commission, Office of the Secretary, 600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Suite CC-5610 (Annex C), Washington, DC 20580. Online: FTC's Rulemaking Docket at regulations.gov (Docket FTC-2023-0007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regulations.gov docket FTC-2023-0007 for online filing or the listed physical address for mail submissions. Ensure the submission is routed to the correct docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Information in Each Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission must include: Reference to 'Non-Compete Clause Rulemaking, Matter No. P201200' and the submitter's name and state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the docket/matter reference and identify the submitter clearly (name and state) so the comment is properly recorded and attributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support with Industry-Specific Details and Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Business submissions should be supported with pertinent details about the industry in which the business operates, the anticompetitive or procompetitive effects of noncompete clauses in that industry, and positions on the proposed rule and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, industry-specific facts, data, examples, and explanation of how noncompetes affect competition and your workforce; tie assertions to evidence rather than conclusory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule vs. Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to categorically ban noncompetes or adopt modified approaches with rebuttable presumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address whether a total ban or a more tailored approach (e.g., presumptions, carve-outs) is appropriate; weigh benefits and costs and provide evidence/examples to support your recommended approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker/Employer Definitions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how 'worker' and 'employer' are defined in the proposed rule, whether those definitions capture or exclude relevant parties, and propose concrete modifications if needed, with rationale and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation by Worker Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether standards should vary by job function, earnings, or seniority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether noncompete treatment should differ for categories of workers (e.g., executives vs. rank-and-file, high-earning vs. low-earning) and provide industry-specific examples or data to justify differentiated rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchisee Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether franchisor–franchisee noncompetes should be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address inclusion or exclusion of franchisor–franchisee relationships, discuss competitive dynamics in franchising, and provide concrete examples or evidence supporting your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Covenants (NDAs, Non-solicitation, Training-Repayment)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the rule should treat related covenants such as NDAs, non-solicitation agreements, and training-repayment agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether and how related restrictive covenants should be addressed alongside noncompetes; explain implications for protectable business interests and worker mobility, and offer drafting or policy alternatives if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Alternatives to Noncompetes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose and evaluate alternatives (e.g., NDAs, garden-leave, narrow confidentiality provisions, non-solicit tailored to protect legitimate interests) and provide evidence of their effectiveness in your industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice-of-Law Evasion / Jurisdictional Strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer use of jurisdictional strategies to evade state law limitations (choice-of-law evasion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether employers use choice-of-law or forum-selection strategies to avoid stricter state protections, provide examples, and recommend mechanisms to prevent evasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership Thresholds / 25% Business Interest Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the 25% business interest exception should be adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the appropriateness of the 25% ownership exception (or other ownership thresholds), including examples of entities/owners affected and policy reasons for raising/lowering or eliminating the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker Notification of Rescinded Clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether employers should notify workers of rescinded clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address whether and how employers should inform workers if noncompete clauses are rescinded, including timing, form of notice, and any recommended safeguards or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Comments on FTC-Requested Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The FTC specifically requests input on a listed set of topics; comments should target those issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments, explicitly respond to the FTC's specific questions and priority topics (listed above), organizing submissions to map claims/evidence to those requested topics for maximum usefulness to regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive Participation Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: This comment period represents 'the only opportunity for businesses to provide input on the proposed rule,' making substantive participation crucial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide well-reasoned, evidence-backed submissions rather than perfunctory statements; explain industry impacts, propose workable alternatives, and demonstrate practical consequences to influence the rulemaking record.
